facility_roles.quote: The initial experiments operating at the 4 collision regions of PETRA were the JADE [28], Mark-J [29], PLUTO [31] and TASSO [30] detectors.

intervals.label: proposal
intervals.note: Proposal "JADE - Proposal for a Compact Magnetic Detector at PETRA" submitted to DESY management; recommended for approval by the PETRA Research Council in October 1976.
intervals.quote: August JADE proposal submitted to DESY management

intervals.label: recommended for approval; construction and installation
intervals.note: Recommended for approval in October 1976; the paper says construction started right after approval of the project in October 1976 (section 3.2). Table 2 dates the move into the beam to February 1979 (Table 1 and section 3.2 say January 1979) and the first data to March 1979.
intervals.quote: October JADE proposal recommended for approval by PRC

intervals.label: PETRA data taking
intervals.locator: Bethke & Wagner (2022), Table 2 (1979, March); end from Table 2 (1986, Nov. 3)
intervals.note: First data (single electron beam) in March 1979; a beam loss damaged the tracking chamber on 26 March 1979 and data taking resumed in June 1979 after repair. End = 3 November 1986 "shutdown of PETRA and the JADE experiment".
intervals.quote: March first data recorded (single e− -beam, Ebeam = 11.3 GeV)

intervals.label: PETRA shut down; experiment ended
intervals.note: JADE data were later preserved and revived; analyses continued until 2012 and data and software were released in 2022 via the CERN Open Data portal.
intervals.quote: Nov. 3 shutdown of PETRA and the JADE experiment

name: JADE

summary.plain: One of the four original detectors at DESY's PETRA collider, built by groups from Japan, Germany and England (the name comes from the three countries). It recorded e+e- collisions from 1979 to 1986 and contributed three-jet evidence for the gluon and an early measurement of the strong coupling.
summary.technical: JADE (JApan-Deutschland-England): compact magnetic detector with a jet chamber and lead-glass calorimeter, proposal submitted August 1976 (signed by 48 authors); first data March 1979; recorded e⁺e⁻ annihilation at centre-of-mass energies 12-46.7 GeV until PETRA shut down on 3 November 1986; spokesperson R. Felst; data and software released through the CERN Open Data portal in 2022.
